description:
Port upstream prompt-templates.ts to Elixir.

Upstream behavior:
- Load .md files (non-recursive) from ~/.pi/prompts/ and {cwd}/.pi/prompts/
- Parse frontmatter (--- delimited YAML): name (from filename without .md), description (frontmatter or first line ≤60 chars), argument-hint
- Argument substitution in template content:
  - $1, $2, ... → positional args (1-indexed)
  - $@ / $ARGUMENTS → all args joined with space
  - ${@:N} → args from Nth onwards (1-indexed, bash slice)
  - ${@:N:L} → L args starting from N (1-indexed)
  - Replacement is non-recursive (arg values not substituted again)
- Shell-like arg parsing: respects single/double quotes (quoted strings are one arg)
- Expansion: user input starting with "/name args" matches template named "name"

Implementation:
- New module: OctoPi.Coder.PromptTemplates
- load_all/1 — scan global + project dirs for .md files
- parse_template/1 — extract frontmatter, name, description, argument_hint
- parse_args/1 — bash-style arg parsing respecting single/double quotes
- substitute_args/2 — apply $1/$@/$ARGUMENTS/${@:N}/${@:N:L} substitutions
- expand/2 — check if text starts with "/name ..." and expand if template found

Tests (TDD — port upstream tests from packages/coding-agent/test/prompt-templates.test.ts):
- Load templates from directory
- Frontmatter name override
- Description from frontmatter vs first line truncation
- $1 substitution
- $@ and $ARGUMENTS substitution
- ${@:2} slicing
- ${@:2:3} slicing
- Quoted args parsing ("hello world" → one arg)
- /template-name expansion
- No match → original text returned
- Empty args for template with $1 → empty string
